points.description: States that empirical equations are derived from experiments or observed data (not from theory or first principles).
points.partial_credit: Mentions data or observation only vaguely, without saying the equation is derived from it.

points.description: States that empirical equations have no mathematical proof behind them (they are not proven or derived theoretically).
points.partial_credit: Says they are 'not theoretical' or 'not exact' without stating that there is no mathematical proof.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) require both the experimental or observed-data origin and the statement that there is no mathematical proof behind the equation. Each element is worth 1 mark and is all or nothing at harsh level, except where the partial credit note applies. A student who gives only one of the two ideas gets 1 mark; a student who gives neither, or gives a wrong statement such as "they are proven by theory", gets 0.
